```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(onet2r)
library(dplyr)
```

[OpenAI Signals](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-expanding-world-of-work/)
classifies consumer ChatGPT work messages into O&#42;NET Intermediate Work
Activities (IWAs). These data describe activities people bring to ChatGPT.
They do not measure the occupation of each user, successful task completion,
or how much AI changes a job.

`onet_openai_iwa_read()` reads the country-quarter IWA CSV you already have.
It does not download data, choose an exposure score, or allocate usage to
occupations. This development feature is intended for a future CRAN update.

## An offline example with declared expectations

**Every share below is invented.** The fixture is a format demonstration,
not a finding about U.S. or British ChatGPT use.

```{r read-invented}
path <- system.file("extdata", "openai-iwa-synthetic.csv", package = "onet2r")
usage <- onet_openai_iwa_read(path, as_of = "invented teaching example")
stopifnot(
  nrow(usage) == 9L,
  n_distinct(usage$country_code) == 2L,
  n_distinct(usage$quarter) == 2L,
  sum(usage$is_other_iwa) == 3L,
  sum(usage$share_of_messages == 0) == 1L,
  all(is.na(usage$iwa_id[usage$is_other_iwa]))
)
knitr::kable(usage |>
  select(quarter, country_code, iwa_category, share_of_messages))
```

The expected output has **nine rows**, **two countries**, **two quarters**,
**three `Other IWA` rows**, and **one reported zero**. Britain has no second
quarter in this invented file. That missing group is not evidence of zero use.

## Keep the denominator and the published precision

The source defines each share as the fraction of classified work-related
messages in a particular country and quarter assigned to an IWA category.
It is not a share of all ChatGPT messages or a share of workers.

```{r inspect-totals}
totals <- usage |>
  summarise(
    reported_categories = n(),
    published_share_sum = sum(share_of_messages),
    .by = c(country_code, quarter)
  )
stopifnot(
  nrow(totals) == 3L,
  all(totals$reported_categories == 3L),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    totals$published_share_sum[
      totals$country_code == "US" & totals$quarter == "2025-04-01"
    ], 0.99999
  ))
)
knitr::kable(totals, digits = 5)
```

The invented second-quarter U.S. sum is **0.99999**, not exactly one.
The reader preserves it. The actual release normalizes after adding
differential-privacy noise, then rounds IWA shares to five decimal places.
Neither small discrepancies nor reported zeros justify reconstructing
unobserved messages. Partial groups can also have lower sums, so totals
alone do not prove completeness.

## Separate named activities from the residual category

`iwa_category` preserves the source label. `iwa_id` contains a joinable
identifier only for a named activity, while `is_other_iwa` marks the residual.

```{r other-category}
other <- usage |> filter(is_other_iwa)
stopifnot(nrow(other) == 3L, all(is.na(other$iwa_id)))
knitr::kable(other |> select(country_code, quarter, iwa_category, share_of_messages))
```

To look up names, use an explicitly selected O&#42;NET archive's
`GWAs to IWAs to DWAs` reference table, read through
`onet_archive_reference()`. Its `iwa_element_id` is the matching activity
key. First make a unique IWA-name lookup and check unmatched source IDs.
Do not join directly to the full reference table without accounting for its
multiple DWA rows per IWA.

IWAs are shared across occupations. A named IWA match tells you which jobs
list an activity, not which workers sent the messages. The same usage share
must not be interpreted as an occupation-specific adoption rate simply
because it can be joined to several occupations.

## Use your downloaded release

Extract only
`public_release_csv/share_of_work_related_messages_by_onet_iwa_country_quarter.csv`
from the Signals ZIP, then pass its local path to `onet_openai_iwa_read()`.
An optional `expected_sha256` pins the extracted CSV, not the ZIP.
`source_url` and `as_of` record metadata you supply. The reader's timestamp
means local read time, not the original download time.

The README version 3.0 supplied with the November 2026 download specifies
CC BY 4.0. Cite OpenAI Signals, preserve attribution, and identify the
snapshot. The package does not bundle real usage rows.

The inspected release has 164 named IWAs plus `Other IWA` across 94 countries,
with unequal country coverage over seven quarters. Consumer messages from
adult accounts are sampled. Enterprise and Codex use are excluded, as are
deleted accounts and users opting out of training. Those coverage boundaries
matter when comparing the data with employment statistics.

## How this differs from TaskNet and exposure studies

TaskNet supplies an alternative inventory of occupational statements.
Signals supplies a distribution of classified consumer work messages.
Published exposure studies supply estimates under their own definitions.
These are different research objects. onet2r records their keys, values,
and provenance without treating one as a substitute for another.
